intro: A quieter news cycle sees AI stories clustered around regulation of chatbots and child safety, a notable Anthropic-assisted math breakthrough, and growing friction between media/trust concerns and AI-infused creative tools, alongside a long-horizon infrastructure bet tied to AI compute demand.

stories.title: New York state bans AI chatbot toys for kids
stories.what_happened: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a five-year ban on selling AI chatbot toys that use internet connectivity to converse with children, including dolls and robots. The law carries fines of $15,000 per day per violation, enforced by the state attorney general.
stories.why_it_matters: This is one of the first state-level bans targeting AI-enabled consumer products specifically marketed to children, reflecting growing legislative anxiety about chatbot safety for minors following high-profile incidents involving companion AI apps. It sets a template other states may follow, potentially forcing toy manufacturers to redesign or pull AI-enabled products from shelves ahead of the holiday season, and signals that child-safety concerns are becoming a primary vector for AI regulation in the absence of federal rules.
stories.watch_next: Watch whether other states introduce similar bans before the holiday shopping season, and how toy manufacturers respond to compliance deadlines.
stories.summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a five-year ban on selling AI chatbot toys that use internet connectivity to converse with children, including dolls and robots. The law carries fines of $15,000 per day per violation, enforced by the state attorney general.

stories.title: State AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from auctioning off users' chat histories
stories.what_happened: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is moving to block Character.AI from auctioning off user chat histories and other sensitive data as part of its bankruptcy proceedings. Officials say the data includes explicit conversations involving children. Character.AI filed for bankruptcy last month amid ongoing lawsuits and investigations into its safety record.
stories.why_it_matters: This case tests how data privacy protections hold up when an AI company facing safety litigation enters bankruptcy and tries to monetize its most sensitive asset — user conversation logs. If the sale proceeds, it could set a troubling precedent for distressed AI companies treating chat data as a liquidatable asset regardless of how it was collected or who it involves. The outcome will likely influence how future AI-companion startups structure data governance and how bankruptcy courts treat consumer AI data going forward.
stories.watch_next: Watch the bankruptcy court's ruling on whether the data sale can proceed and whether this prompts federal action on AI data protections during corporate dissolution.
stories.summary: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is moving to block Character.AI from auctioning off user chat histories and other sensitive data as part of its bankruptcy proceedings. Officials say the data includes explicit conversations involving children. Character.AI filed for bankruptcy last month amid ongoing lawsuits and investigations into its safety record.

stories.title: Much shorter version of GRH Lean verification from Anthropic
stories.what_happened: Anthropic released a shortened Lean 4 formal verification of the Riemann Hypothesis and Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, built on Mathlib and produced in collaboration between Anthropic researchers and Claude. The compact version runs about 76,000 lines versus roughly 300,000 for the readable edition, based on prior work by mathematician Levent Alpöge.
stories.why_it_matters: A machine-assisted formal proof touching one of mathematics' most consequential open problems — even if building on existing human mathematical insight rather than proving RH outright — demonstrates how far AI-assisted formal verification has progressed in compressing and mechanizing extremely long, rigorous proofs. It's a concrete signal that frontier AI models are becoming genuinely useful collaborators in formal theorem-proving at a scale previously requiring large human teams, with implications for verified software, cryptography, and the broader Lean/Mathlib ecosystem.
stories.watch_next: Watch for peer scrutiny of the proof's scope and claims, and whether other research groups apply similar Claude-assisted compression techniques to other major formalization efforts.
stories.summary: Anthropic released a shortened Lean 4 formal verification of the Riemann Hypothesis and Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, built on Mathlib and produced in collaboration between Anthropic researchers and Claude. The compact version runs about 76,000 lines versus roughly 300,000 for the readable edition, based on prior work by mathematician Levent Alpöge.

stories.title: SpaceX wins FCC approval to deploy 1M orbital data center satellites
stories.what_happened: The FCC approved SpaceX's application to deploy up to one million orbital data center satellites, with the first launches targeted for as early as 2028. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr tied the approval explicitly to extending America's lead in AI compute, referring to it using the administration's preferred term "Super Intelligence."
stories.why_it_matters: This marks a major regulatory green light for moving AI compute infrastructure into orbit, a concept long considered speculative. If realized at scale, space-based data centers could reshape assumptions about power, cooling, and land constraints that currently bottleneck AI buildout on Earth, while also raising new questions about orbital debris, security, and international competition for space-based compute dominance. The unusually fast ten-month approval timeline also signals how aggressively US regulators are now prioritizing AI infrastructure approvals.
stories.watch_next: Watch for SpaceX's technical roadmap details, any competing satellite data center proposals from rivals, and international regulatory reactions to a potential US orbital compute buildout.
stories.summary: The FCC approved SpaceX's application to deploy up to one million orbital data center satellites, with the first launches targeted for as early as 2028. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr tied the approval explicitly to extending America's lead in AI compute, referring to it using the administration's preferred term "Super Intelligence."

stories.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
stories.what_happened: The New York Times instructed freelance photographers not to update to the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because new AI features embed metadata identifying images as AI-generated in ways that may not be obvious to users. The warning came in an email from two Times photography leaders, seen by The Verge.
stories.why_it_matters: This highlights a growing trust problem at the intersection of creative tools and AI: as generative features get baked into ubiquitous software like Photoshop by default, even non-AI-assisted work risks being mislabeled or contaminated with AI provenance metadata, undermining journalistic authenticity standards. It signals that major publishers are now treating AI feature creep in standard tools as an operational risk requiring explicit internal policy, which could push Adobe and other software vendors toward clearer opt-in/opt-out controls and transparent metadata practices.
stories.watch_next: Watch for Adobe's response on metadata controls and whether other news organizations issue similar internal guidance restricting AI-enabled creative software.
stories.summary: The New York Times instructed freelance photographers not to update to the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because new AI features embed metadata identifying images as AI-generated in ways that may not be obvious to users. The warning came in an email from two Times photography leaders, seen by The Verge.
